executive_summary.question: If a person intends to kill one individual but instead unintentionally causes the death of a different person, how is the resulting culpable homicide classified?
executive_summary.generated_answer:
Under the provision dealing with transferred intent (Section 102), if a person intends—or knows is likely—to cause the death of one individual but, by the same act, unintentionally causes the death of another person, the culpable homicide is **classified exactly as it would have been had the intended victim been killed**.  

In other words, the offense retains the same legal description (murder or culpable homicide not amounting to murder) that it would have had if the death had occurred to the person whose death the offender intended or knew was likely to cause.  

*Source:* Section 102 states:  
> “If a person, by doing anything which he intends or knows to be likely to cause death, commits culpable homicide by causing the death of any person, whose death he neither intends nor knows himself to be likely to cause, the culpable homicide committed by the offender is of the description of which it would have been if he had caused the death of the person whose death he intended or knew himself to be likely to cause.”【ac6c1423-8651-4ff8-9f26-0cf720a5f981】.
